subject: Learning Methods
title: Diagnosing What You Don't Know
description: A quick win: understand Diagnosing What You Don't Know.

hook.text: A medical student could name every bone but couldn't explain how joints work. She had facts without connections.

buildup.text: Knowledge gaps come in two types: missing facts and missing connections between facts. Both need different fixes.

discovery.text: Teaching reveals connection gaps that self-testing may miss. A question asks 'what.' An explanation asks 'why and how.'

twist.text: Most students study facts and ignore connections. This is why they can pass quizzes but fail application questions.

climax.text: After learning facts, explain the connections between them. How does A cause B? Why does C prevent D?

punchline.text: Know the facts, then explain the connections between them.

quiz.question: What type of knowledge gap does teaching reveal that self-testing may miss?
